# Siddhidatri v0 — three detectors, one calibrated verdict

**SMD (Server Machine Dataset)** (NetManAIOps/OmniAnomaly @ `7fb0e0acf89e`), 28 real servers. Siddhidatri is a logistic regression over shailaputri, max robust z, pca. Its weights are learned on Shailaputri's *out-of-fold* scores inside the training groups, so the fusion never trusts a model scored on its own training data. Each machine group is held out in turn. Each single detector is also given its own logistic calibration, so every row states a probability.

## Mean across held-out machine groups

| Verdict from | F1 | Episode recall | False alarms / 1000 | ECE ↓ | Brier ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **siddhidatri-v0** | 0.534 | 0.768 | 47.9 | 0.0419 | 0.0571 |
| shailaputri | 0.530 | 0.590 | 4.0 | 0.0183 | 0.0415 |
| max robust z | 0.253 | 0.778 | 20.4 | 0.0183 | 0.0420 |
| pca | 0.416 | 0.724 | 84.5 | 0.0422 | 0.0582 |

## How to read this

- **ECE** (expected calibration error) is the average gap between the probability stated and the rate observed. 0 means a verdict of 80% is right 80% of the time. **Brier** is the mean squared error of the probabilities.
- A large weight on one detector means the others add little *on these servers*. That is a finding, not a failure.
